content.title: 98th Academy Awards: How & Where to Watch Tonight's 2026 Oscars
content.text: THE OSCARS® "The Oscars" will be held on Sunday, March 2, 2025, at the Dolby® Theatre at Ovation Hollywood and will air live on ABC, Hulu and broadcast outlets in more than 200 territories worldwide. (Disney/Frank Micelotta) CONAN O'BRIEN (Photo by Frank Micelotta/Disney via Getty Images)Disney via Getty ImagesHollywood’s biggest night is finally here. The 98th Academy Awards take place tonight, Sunday, March 15, at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles — and whether you have a horse in the race, a favorite film or actor you’re rooting for, a musical performance you’re excited to watch, or you’re just curious about the nominees, here's everything you need to know before the show.When Do The Oscars Start?The ceremony kicks off at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT, running slightly earlier than in previous years. Plan for roughly three to four hours of airtime.Where To Watch And Stream The 2026 OscarsThe Academy Awards air live on ABC and stream live on Hulu for all subscribers. If you've cut the cord, any service that carries ABC will work, including YouTube TV, FuboTV, AT&T TV, and DirecTV Stream.PROMOTEDRed Carpet Pre-ShowThe official red carpet pre-show begins at 6:30 p.m. ET / 3:30 p.m. PT on ABC and Hulu, hosted by Tamron Hall and Jesse Palmer. E! will also have its traditional live coverage starting earlier in the day at 2 p.m. ET / 11 a.m. PT.Be sure to check out my other streaming recommendations for this weekend right here.MORE FOR YOUForbesWhat To Watch This Weekend: New Shows And Movies To Stream On Netflix, Hulu, Prime Video, Apple TV And MoreBy Erik KainHost And AnnouncerConan O’Brien returns for his second consecutive year as host, following a well-received debut in 2025. He’s described the preparation as a "running battle" right up until showtime, with promises of some more ambitious ideas than last year. Email Address O’Brien says he’s been practicing his Oscars routine at comedy clubs to work out the kinks. "The crowds really like it, because I’m a surprise, so they don’t know that I’m gonna show up," O’Brien said recently on Good Morning America. "And some of these are very far-flung comedy clubs. They're also a bowling alley. They're also a car rental place."I’m always happy to see O’Brien given the spotlight, as he’s just genuinely one of the funniest and nicest people in the business.Matt Berry, best known as Laszlo in the hilarious vampire comedy, What We Do in the Shadows, will serve as the ceremony’s announce – a genuinely inspired choice. The things that man can do with his voice. I’m not sure the Oscars audience is ready.Musical PerformersTwo of the five Best Original Song nominees will be performed live tonight, chosen for their "global cultural impact and audience connection.""Golden" from KPop Demon Hunters will be performed by EJAE (Kim Eun-jae), Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami — the voices behind the film’s HUNTR/X KPop group — alongside a fusion of traditional Korean instrumentalists and dancers."I Lied to You" from Sinners will be performed by actor Miles Caton and co-songwriter Raphael Saadiq in what’s being described as a sprawling homage to the film’s visual style. The pair will be joined onstage by Misty Copeland, Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone "Kingfish" Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush, Shaboozey and Alice Smith. This song, and the striking, surrealist sequence during the film, was one of the coolest experiences I’ve ever had at a movie theater; a testament both to the power of the big screen and the capacity for music and film to transport us in profound and unexpected ways. Josh Groban and the Los Angeles Master Chorale will also appear during the broadcast.The three Best Song nominees that won't be performed tonight are Nick Cave and Bryce Dessner's "Train Dreams," Diane Warren's "Dear Me," and "Sweet Dreams of Joy" from Viva Verdi!I’m a little sad that Nick Cave and Bryce Dessner (of The National) won’t be performing “Train Dreams” as they’re some of my favorite musical artists, so here’s the song’s music video:PresentersQuite the list of A-listers will take the stage at this year’s Oscars to present awards. Last year's acting winners — Adrien Brody, Kieran Culkin, Mikey Madison and Zoe Saldaña — all return to the stage as presenters. They're joined by Will Arnett, Javier Bardem, Rose Byrne, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Anne Hathaway, Chase Infiniti, Nicole Kidman, Jimmy Kimmel, Delroy Lindo, Ewan McGregor, Paul Mescal, Demi Moore, Wagner Moura, Kumail Nanjiani, Gwyneth Paltrow, Pedro Pascal, Bill Pullman, Lewis Pullman, Maya Rudolph, Channing Tatum and Sigourney Weaver.Special Moments To Watch ForTonight’s show has a few extras in store that should be a fun addition to Conan O’Brien’s hosting gags. A Bridesmaids cast reunion will bring together Rose Byrne, Kristen Wiig, Maya Rudolph and Melissa McCarthy. There will also be a Marvel reunion featuring Robert Downey Jr. (aka both Iron Man and Doctor Doom) and Chris Evans (Captain America), who both return in this year’s upcoming MCU event film, Avengers: Doomsday, in December. Producers have also teased an "extraterrestrial" guest taking the stage, but have kept said alien’s identity a secret. E.T.? Baby Yoda? We shall see . . . .On the tribute front, Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan will reunite to honor the late Rob Reiner, the director of When Harry Met Sally which Crystal and Ryan starred in (among other terrific films) and Barbra Streisand is reportedly set to perform a tribute to Robert Redford.ForbesThe Top 5 Rob Reiner Movies, From ‘Spinal Tap’ To ‘The Princess Bride’By Erik KainKey Nominees: What To WatchSinners is the runaway frontrunner heading into tonight, having broken the all-time record for most Oscar nominations ever with 16 nods — surpassing the previous record of 14 held by Titanic, La La Land and All About Eve. Ryan Coogler’s vampire drama could make history in more ways than one. Cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw could become the first woman to win Best Cinematography, and costume designer Ruth E. Carter could become the first black three-time Oscar winner.Sinners has been nominated widely across awards season, but has also been widely snubbed, especially at this year’s Golden Globes, where One Battle After Another dominated.The Paul Thomas Anderson film (and my personal pick for Best Picture) sits in second place with 13 nominations, followed by Marty Supreme, Frankenstein and Sentimental Value with nine apiece, and Hamnet with eight.2026 Oscar NomineesBest PictureBugoniaF1FrankensteinHamnetMarty SupremeOne Battle After AnotherThe Secret AgentSentimental ValueSinners (record 16 nominations)Train DreamsBest DirectorPaul Thomas Anderson — One Battle After AnotherRyan Coogler — SinnersJosh Safdie — Marty SupremeJoachim Trier — Sentimental ValueChloé Zhao — HamnetBest ActorTimothée Chalamet — Marty SupremeLeonardo DiCaprio — One Battle After AnotherEthan Hawke — Blue MoonMichael B. New This Year: Best CastingThe 2026 ceremony introduces a brand new category — Best Casting — making it the 24th competitive award at the Oscars. The inaugural nominees are Nina Gold (Hamnet), Jennifer Venditti (Marty Supreme), Cassandra Kulukundis (One Battle After Another), Gabriel Domingues (The Secret Agent) and Francine Maisler (Sinners).The 98th Academy Awards air tonight at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT on ABC and Hulu.
